# Reachable volatiles in gen9 randbats — EVALUATOR_SPEC gate 1

*Generated by `evallab/rbpool.py`. Do not hand-edit; re-run it.*

The engine's `PokemonVolatileStatus` enum has **107** variants. **44** are reachable in gen9 randbats and get a column; **63** are excluded.

Pool: 509 species, 5851 sets, 349 distinct moves, 60 items, 203 abilities, 19 tera types, levels 64-100.

Evidence classes: `data/move`, `data/secondary`, `data/self` are read straight out of `foul-play/data/moves.json` for moves that are in the pool. `data/charge` is a two-turn move. `mechanic` is a gen9 rule the JSON does not express, named with the pool move that triggers it. `ability` is a pool ability that causes it -- either one of the same name, or a name-MISMATCHED cause listed in `ABILITY_CAUSES` (Cute Charm -> ATTRACT, Electromorphosis -> CHARGE). `engine` is always-on.

The count is 44 either way; the membership moved. Re-running the enumeration moves nothing else.*

# AUDIT VERDICT (independent re-derivation, 2026-08-14)

*Appendix written by an external audit, not by `rbpool.py`. Re-running `rbpool.py`
overwrites this file — fix `rbpool.py` first (see "Root cause" below), then re-run.*

Method: engine volatile enum read from `poke-engine/src/genx/state.rs:171` (107
variants). Pool re-derived from `foul-play/data/pkmn_sets_cache/gen9randombattle.json`
and **cross-checked against the read-only ground truth**
`pokemon-showdown/data/random-battles/gen9/sets.json`: the two agree exactly on
349 moves and 203 abilities across 509 species (zero symmetric difference), so the
cache is a faithful pool. Causes were then derived from the engine source itself —
every `ApplyVolatileStatus` / `volatile_status:` / `Effect::VolatileStatus` write site
in `choices.rs`, `genx/abilities.rs`, `genx/items.rs`, `genx/contact_reactions.rs`,
`genx/choice_effects.rs`, `genx/generate_instructions.rs` — attributed to its owning
move / ability / item, then intersected with the pool.

**Result: 40 of the 44 admissions and 61 of the 63 exclusions are correct.
Four disagreements — 2 misses (real mechanics invisible to the evaluator) and
2 dead columns.**

## Disagreement 1 — ATTRACT: excluded, but REACHABLE (miss)

| | |
|---|---|
| Cause | ability **Cute Charm** (`Abilities::CUTECHARM`, `genx/abilities.rs:4435-4473`) |
| Carrier | **enamorus** — 2 of its 5 randbats sets, **49.7 %** of its set weight |
| Effect | 30 % chance on any contact hit to apply ATTRACT **to the attacker** |

The engine implements this as a first-class contact reaction: `CUTECHARM` injects a
`Secondary { chance: 30.0, target: User, effect: VolatileStatus(ATTRACT) }`, and
`genx/contact_reactions.rs:220-232` lists `VolatileStatus(ATTRACT)` in
`is_contact_reaction_effect`. The engine's own comments name the case explicitly:
"reachable in gen9 randbats: Whiscash's Liquidation into a Cute Charm Enamorus", and
`genx/generate_instructions.rs:1250-1258` calls the Cute Charm Enamorus "the format's
only attract source". A measured synth game (synth731752 T9) is cited in-source with
PS printing `|-start|p2a: Salamence|Attract|[from] ability: Cute Charm`. The
`attract` move being absent from the pool is irrelevant.

## Disagreement 2 — CHARGE: excluded, but REACHABLE (miss)

| | |
|---|---|
| Cause | ability **Electromorphosis** (`Abilities::ELECTROMORPHOSIS`, `genx/abilities.rs:1736-1756`) |
| Carrier | **bellibolt** — **100 %** of its randbats sets (4 of 4) |
| Effect | being hit for damage grants the holder CHARGE, which **doubles its next Electric move** (`genx/damage_calc.rs:2950`) |

Wind Power (`genx/abilities.rs:1758-1785`) is a second CHARGE source but is not in the
pool. Electromorphosis alone makes CHARGE reachable, and it is a damage-doubling
flag — exactly the kind of state the evaluator must not be blind to. The `charge`
move being absent from the pool is irrelevant.

## Disagreements 3 and 4 — LIGHTSCREEN and REFLECT: admitted, but UNREACHABLE (dead columns)

In this engine the LIGHTSCREEN and REFLECT **volatiles** are gen1-only. `choices.rs`
sets them under `if cfg!(feature = "gen1")` (`choices.rs:9777-9795` and
`13611-13629`); the gen9 branch of each move sets a **side condition** instead, and no
other write site for either variant exists anywhere in `genx/`. foul-play agrees —
`fp/search/poke_engine_helpers.py:815` passes reflect/light screen as
`side_conditions`, never as volatiles. Both are already encoded as
`SIDE_CONDITION_FIELDS` (`light_screen`, `reflect`), so these two volatile columns are
**always zero**: no information is lost, but 2 of 44 columns are dead.

## Root cause in `rbpool.py`

Both misses come from one gap and both dead columns from one over-broad rule:

* `enumerate_volatiles` step 2 admits an ability only when **the ability name equals
  the volatile name** (`if ab.upper() in evidence`). Cute Charm→ATTRACT and
  Electromorphosis→CHARGE are name-mismatched ability causes and are therefore never
  considered. `MECHANIC_CAUSES["ATTRACT"]` lists only the move `attract`, and
  `MECHANIC_CAUSES["CHARGE"]` only the move `charge`.
  Fix: add `("ability", "cutecharm", ...)` to `ATTRACT` and
  `("ability", "electromorphosis", ...)` to `CHARGE`.
* Step 1's "a volatile named exactly after a pool move" rule fires for `lightscreen`
  and `reflect`, which are gen9 side conditions. Fix: add both to
  `STRUCTURAL_EXCLUSIONS` ("side condition in gen9; volatile variant is gen1-only").

Neither volatile carries a duration (`VolatileStatusDurations`, `state.rs:890-907`, has
no attract/charge field), so the fix is +2 bit columns, -2 dead columns — net 44 columns
either way, with a different membership.

## Other admissions spot-checked and confirmed (evidence nits only, reachability correct)

* **TRAPPED** — reachable, but the stated evidence is wrong in both halves. The engine
  never writes a TRAPPED volatile for Arena Trap / Shadow Tag / Magnet Pull (those are
  legality checks in `genx/state.rs:1037`); the only writer is the **spiritshackle**
  move (`choices.rs:16170`), carried by **decidueye**.
* **CUDCHEW** — reachable and actually triggerable: taurospaldeaaqua / taurospaldeablaze
  carry Cud Chew **with sitrusberry**.
* **UNBURDEN** — reachable and triggerable: hawlucha / hitmonlee / sneasler with
  whiteherb, drifblim with sitrusberry.
* **Charging moves** — confirmed exactly two: `solarbeam` (ninetales, sunflora, torkoal)
  and `meteorbeam` (armarouge, eternatus, glimmora, ironjugulis). Every other member of
  `charge_choice_to_volatile` (`choice_effects.rs:3249`) is out of pool.
* **MUSTRECHARGE** — `gigaimpact` (slaking) is the pool's only recharge move.
* **CONFUSION** — the md lists 3 triggers; `waterpulse` (clawitzer) and `alluringvoice`
  (alcremie, `choice_effects.rs`) are two more. Evidence rows are examples, so this is
  not an error.

## Encoder wiring (gate 6)

`evallab/enc2.py:100-105` takes `VOL_COLS = rbpool.reachable_list()` directly and writes
all `len(VOL_COLS)` columns contiguously at `enc2.py:885-886`, with the 13 matching
duration fields at `887-889`. Re-running `rbpool.enumerate_volatiles()` reproduces
exactly the 44/63 split in this file. **The enumeration is fully wired through — the
encoder encodes precisely what the enumeration admits, no more and no less.** It
therefore inherits both misses: ATTRACT and CHARGE currently have no column.
